A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HERMES and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original HERMES benchmark results, component ablations, latency measurements and qualitative analyses, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds VideoMME integration experiments, memory measurements and further ablations.

M1.justification: The matched ECO merging algorithm, query compression, SeTR procedure and Q-Former/Vicuna pipeline remain unchanged. H.3.1 newly documents positional encoding before ECO, but does not establish that this represents a revision to the earlier procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds VideoMME evaluation without subtitles for the plug-in experiments. This extends coverage within video question answering; the existing LVU, Breakfast, COIN and MovieChat-1k tasks and datasets remain.

E2.justification: The plug-in comparisons expand substantially from MA-LMM alone to include unmodified LongVA-7B and LLaVA-OneVision-7B controls and their augmented variants (v4 Tables 3–5). K-Means is also added to the semantic-compression comparison in Table 7. Comparator membership in the original standalone benchmarks is retained.

E3.justification: The added VideoMME experiments introduce zero-shot evaluation without subtitles using 7B models, batch size 1, 128 frames, 32 episodes and a 0.125 keep ratio. GPU memory becomes an evaluation measure. The documented settings for the original experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a K-Means compression comparison, an ablation isolating positional encoding, and a visualization of extracted semantics versus episodes (Figure 12). Existing frame-count, window-size, episode-count and keep-ratio analyses, along with the failure cases, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests or uncertainty estimates for its experimental results.

E6.justification: v4 adds a substantial block of VideoMME accuracy, latency and memory results. Baseline/ECO/ECO-plus-SeTR accuracies are 54.11/54.19/54.56 for LongVA and 58.26/58.93/59.30 for LLaVA-OneVision. New results also include MA-LMM memory measurements, K-Means at 75.7 accuracy and 4.11 score, and 77.3 accuracy without positional encoding versus 78.6 with it. Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and compression algorithm are substantively unchanged. Equations are relocated or expressed with equivalent notation, including using U for the projected representation in Equation 8. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: v4 elevates and broadens the existing off-the-shelf integration claim into a central contribution alongside standalone HERMES. The abstract and contributions now emphasize applicability across existing models and headline reductions of up to 43% in latency and 46% in GPU memory; the conclusion extends the claims to five datasets and three integration models.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section identifies heuristic compression failures, possible redundancy between independently operating modules, and pretraining constraints limiting direct comparisons. H.3.1 adds explanations involving positional encoding and implicit event-frequency retention. The earlier failure analyses and cognitive interpretation remain.

D1.justification: v4 specifies which modules are fine-tuned, confirms inference-only insertion without additional training, provides VideoMME hyperparameters, and documents pre-ECO positional encoding. Its abstract now describes code as available, although H.1 retains future-release wording, leaving availability internally ambiguous.

R1.justification: Targeted additions cover temporal-difference and event-adaptive networks, low-bitrate video coding, Transformer-XL, Compressive Transformer, VideoMME and the new integration models. The BLIP-2 reference is removed. H.5 expands distinctions from MA-LMM and MovieChat while retaining the established cognitive positioning.

P1.justification: Related work moves ahead of the problem statement, the problem and framework introductions are reorganized, and the abstract, contributions and conclusion are substantially rewritten around modular integration. Plug-in experiments receive a separate pilot-study section, limitations become a main section, and the appendix is reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Classification tables are merged, integration tables are added, and the efficiency chart and qualitative Figure 6 are redesigned. Figure 1 is replaced, a new module visualization becomes Figure 12, and the retained failure figure becomes Figure 13.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens v3's MA-LMM-only integration evidence with two additional model families and measured memory costs. The positional-encoding ablation, implementation disclosures and specific limitations improve scrutiny. These are useful but bounded gains: the original standalone evidence is unchanged, the small new accuracy differences lack uncertainty estimates, and conflicting code-release statements introduce a documentation weakness.
